content.text: Can you explain scaled dot-product attention? Why do we divide by the square root of d_k?

chat_messages.text:
Attention lets every token build its representation as a weighted mix of all other tokens. Each token is projected into a **query** \(q\), a **key** \(k\) and a **value** \(v\):

$$
\mathrm{Attention}(Q, K, V) = \mathrm{softmax}\left(\frac{QK^\top}{\sqrt{d_k}}\right) V
$$

### Why divide by \(\sqrt{d_k}\)?

If the components of \(q\) and \(k\) are independent with mean 0 and variance 1, their dot product \(q \cdot k = \sum_{i=1}^{d_k} q_i k_i\) has variance \(d_k\). For large \(d_k\) the logits get huge, softmax saturates and gradients vanish. Dividing by \(\sqrt{d_k}\) brings the variance back to 1.

A minimal NumPy version:

```python
import numpy as np

def attention(Q: np.ndarray, K: np.ndarray, V: np.ndarray) -> np.ndarray:
    d_k = Q.shape[-1]
    scores = Q @ K.T / np.sqrt(d_k)
    weights = np.exp(scores - scores.max(axis=-1, keepdims=True))
    weights /= weights.sum(axis=-1, keepdims=True)
    return weights @ V
```

| Shape | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `Q: (n, d_k)` | one query per token |
| `K: (m, d_k)` | one key per token attended to |
| `V: (m, d_v)` | values that get mixed |
| output `(n, d_v)` | new representation per query |
And multi-head attention is just several of these in parallel?

content.text: And multi-head attention is just several of these in parallel?

chat_messages.text:
Exactly. With \(h\) heads, each head has its own projections \(W_i^Q, W_i^K, W_i^V\) into a smaller space \(d_k = d_{model} / h\). The heads run in parallel, their outputs are concatenated and projected once more:

\[ \mathrm{MultiHead}(Q,K,V) = \mathrm{Concat}(\mathrm{head}_1, \dots, \mathrm{head}_h) W^O \]

The total cost is about the same as one full-width head, but each head can specialise, e.g. one tracks syntax, another coreference.
